title: Integrating Small Satellite Missions into a Multi-Mission Operations Environment: A Consolidated Approach with EGS-CC
short_title: Integrating small satellites at GSOC with EGS-CC (4S 2024)
organisation: German Space Operations Center (GSOC), Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR); presented at The 4S Symposium 2024
status_notes: Conference paper for The 4S Symposium 2024 (page footers, e.g. PDF p. 1). No version or status information is printed.
summary:
A conference paper from DLR's German Space Operations Center (GSOC) on how to operate New Space small satellites inside a multi-mission environment built on CCSDS and ECSS standards. It first describes the GSOC set-up: **GECCOS**, a [SCOS-2000](../scos2000/index.md)-based mission control system, connects through the NCTRS protocol to an SLE Switch Board and from there to a worldwide ground station network over [SLE](../ccsds/sle/index.md). Procedures are prepared and run with ProToS, and telemetry is monitored with SATMON. Under this approach the spacecraft manufacturer has to deliver a [MIB](../mib/index.md) and operations procedures.

The case study is **CubeL**, a 3U CubeSat launched in early 2021 that uses the CubeSat Space Protocol (CSP) rather than CCSDS packets and [PUS](../ecss/pus/index.md), and came without a MIB. Integrating it took custom work on both the space and ground segments: a patched modem firmware, a new S-band commanding tool, an auxiliary MIB and a new offline-processing tool.

The proposed alternative uses **EGS-CC**, the planned replacement for GECCOS. Its domain-agnostic kernel is adapted to a mission by an exchangeable Reference Implementation (RI) and by the Tailoring Data Model (TDM). The authors define a CSP RI in which an EGS-CC activity processor calls the manufacturer's CSP C API through SWIG-generated Java/JNI bindings packaged as Karaf bundles. A prototype commanded CubeL in January 2024. The paper ends with an outlook on multiple RIs side by side, a project-specific software modem at the ground-station interface, and how requirements on manufacturers might change (exposing an API instead of delivering a MIB).

key_points.text: GSOC's core mission operations systems and ground station equipment are stated to rely on CCSDS 132.0-B-3, CCSDS 232.0-B-4, CCSDS 133.0-B-2 and ECSS E-ST-70-41C.
GECCOS, the SCOS-2000-based MCS at GSOC, uses the NCTRS protocol to connect to an SLE Switch Board (SSB), which gives access to a worldwide ground station network via SLE.
The two elements described as central to TM/TC communications are the MIB, in which each TM/TC is precisely defined, and the procedures that fix the order in which TCs are sent.
Procedures are prepared and executed with GSOC's ProToS tool suite through the GECCOS API; telemetry is monitored with SATMON, also accessible outside the control centre as SATMON@home.
The paper calls it an 'industry standard' that the manufacturer provides a MIB and the procedures so that SCOS-2000-based systems such as GECCOS can operate the spacecraft.
CubeL (3U CubeSat, launched early 2021) was the first small satellite operated at GSOC; its manufacturer toolkit uses CSP packets over ZMQ with a command-line tool, CSP-Term.

CubeL had no MIB; integrating it required patching the on-board modem firmware, a new S-band commanding tool, an auxiliary MIB for telemetry parsing, a new offline-processing tool and mission-planning changes.
EGS-CC is set to replace GECCOS as the central MCS component at GSOC; its kernel is domain-agnostic and is adapted to an application by a Reference Implementation (RI).
The Tailoring Data Model (TDM) tailors the kernel's abstract Monitoring and Control Model (MCM) into a hierarchy of monitoring and control elements with parameters, events and activities.
In the CSP RI, an activity is routed through the MCA and MCM kernel components to an activity processor that calls the manufacturer's CSP API; the API's return value is mapped to the activity result.

The CSP component is an Apache Maven project with three modules (csp-library, csp-terminal, csp-feature); SWIG generates Java bindings and JNI glue code for the C CSP libraries, deployed in EGS-CC's Apache Karaf OSGi runtime.
A prototype EGS-CC system with a CSP RI commanded CubeL in an experimental pass in January 2024 (pings to the on-board computer and requested housekeeping TM).

For non-CCSDS links the paper proposes routing the RF signal to a project-specific software modem at the operations centre, since the SLE-based ground-station interface and CORTEX hardware rely on CCSDS 401.0, 131.0 and 231.0.

notes: The extraction reports 18 PDF pages while the registry lists 17; the last page appears to be blank. Figures (GSOC mission operations segment, EGS-CC architecture, CSP component design) are images, and only some of their labels survive in the text. The paper cites CCSDS 131.0-B-4, but the current TM coding issue is B-5; this is only a citation in the paper. GECCOS is spelled out as 'GSOC Enhanced Command and Control System for Operating Spacecrafts' in the abbreviation list (PDF p. 16).
